title: Callgraph Harvester — runbook and lightweight CI scripts
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a pragmatic, compact runbook for harvesting user-space callgraphs and lightweight stack traces from the serving runtime with minimal perturbation. The goal is to produce actionable artifacts (callgraphs, flat profiles, annotated flamegraphs) that are CI-friendly and small enough to archive as triage artifacts. Use this when a latency regression or CPU hotspot is suspected but a full continuous-profiling setup is not available.

When to use this:
- Intermittent ~1-5% P99 latency bumps that are hard to reproduce locally
- New kernel or container runtime rollout where we suspect syscalls or scheduler stalls
- Before/after model kernel changes (quantization, fused kernels) to check CPU side effects

High-level strategy:
1) Capture brief live stacks (1–5s) with perf or async-profiler to minimize overhead.
2) For async/IO-heavy regions, collect lightweight eBPF traces (ustack, bpf_trace_printk) limited to specific pids or cgroups.
3) Post-process into folded stacks and generate a flamegraph + a callgraph (dot) for quick visual triage.
4) Commit artifacts to the CI run (artifact store) with metadata: commit, config, workload, seq_len distribution.

Core commands (cheat sheet) — run on an instance with debug symbols available.
- Find PID of process handling request: ps aux | grep runtime-server
- Simple perf record (user-only, low overhead):
  perf record -F 99 -p <PID> -g --sleep 3 --call-graph dwarf && perf script > perf.raw
- Fold stacks for flamegraph (using FlameGraph tools):
  ./stackcollapse-perf.pl perf.raw > perf.folded
  ./flamegraph.pl perf.folded > perf.svg
- perf top for quick hotspots (sampled):
  perf top -p <PID> -H --call-graph dwarf

Low-overhead eBPF ustack sampling (bcc-based) — useful for nanosec syscalls and kernel transitions:
- sudo /usr/share/bcc/tools/stackcount -p <PID> -d 3 > stacks.txt
- Convert to folded form: (quick awk)
  awk 'BEGIN{ORS=""} {gsub(/\t/," "); print $1";"substr($0,index($0,$2))"\n"}' stacks.txt > perf.folded

Async-profiler (JVM/native mixed) — when server has mixed stacks or native threads: 
- Start collector: ./profiler.sh -e cpu -f /tmp/profile.html <PID> 3s
- For flamegraph output: ./profiler.sh -e cpu -o flamegraph -f /tmp/flame.svg <PID>

Generating a callgraph (dot) for hotspot reasoning
- Use gprof2dot on perf output or pprof-compatible profiles:
  perf script | gprof2dot -f perf -o callgraph.dot
  dot -Tsvg callgraph.dot -o callgraph.svg
- Keep dot graphs trimmed to top-20 nodes to avoid noise. Use: gprof2dot ... | head -n 200 > callgraph.dot

CI job pattern (lightweight):
- Trigger: nightly perf smoke or post-merge when PR touches serving runtime
- Job steps (container):
  1) start test harness with same binary and debug symbols
  2) run short synthetic workload (loadgen with recorded seq len distribution) for 30s warmup + 60s sample
  3) run perf record -F 200 -p <PID> -g --call-graph dwarf --sleep 10
  4) produce perf.folded and flame.svg (store artifact)
  5) run a small heuristic script that fails job on new top-N hotspot changes (optional)

Example GitLab CI job snippet (pseudo):
  perf-harvest-nightly:
    image: redwood/profiling-tools:stable
    script:
      - ./start-harness.sh --config ci/harvest-config.yaml &
      - H_PID=$!; sleep 20
      - perf record -F 150 -p $H_PID -g --call-graph dwarf --sleep 8 || true
      - perf script > perf.raw
      - ./stackcollapse-perf.pl perf.raw > perf.folded
      - ./flamegraph.pl perf.folded > perf.svg
      - tar -czf artifacts/perf-$CI_COMMIT_SHA.tgz perf.raw perf.folded perf.svg
    artifacts:
      paths: [artifacts/perf-*.tgz]
      when: always

Artifact metadata to attach (very small JSON):
- commit: $CI_COMMIT_SHA
- binary: sha256:
- kernel: uname -a
- loadgen: name and seed
- seq_len_p50/p90/p99 (string)

Troubleshooting notes & common pitfalls:
- No symbols in flamegraph: ensure build includes -g and we’re running same binary. Use coredump or strip map if container strips symbols.
- perf record permission errors: run in privileged container or setcap cap_sys_admin,cap_perfmon+ep on perf binary; for CI prefer privileged ephemeral runner.
- Excessive overhead on tiny instances: reduce sampling frequency (-F 50) and shorter sample windows.
- eBPF tools require kernel >= 4.9 for many BCC scripts; in older kernels use perf.sample_stack or upgrade kernel image.
- High-frequency noise: collapse kernel frames via --no-children or filter by function prefix (e.g., exclude std::filesystem).

Interpretation heuristics (quick):
- If flamegraph shows long flat wide frames in user space -> CPU bound in compute (look at hot function names).
- Large stacks with many small-cost frames -> scheduler or blocking IO (investigate epoll, futex, select).
- Kernel-heavy stacks -> syscalls: check batching, socket options, sendmsg overhead, and network stack.
- Recurring growth in tail of stacks across runs -> memory fragmentation or GC cycles (if applicable).

Short scripts we keep in repo (descriptions):
- harvest-fast.sh: orchestration wrapper for perf/eBPF + artifact packaging (used in CI).
- fold-and-flame.py: lightweight post-processor that normalizes paths, strips container prefixes, and annotates with model name and seq_len.
- compare-hotspots.py: compares top-50 symbols across two folded profiles and emits delta report.

Follow-ups and next steps (owners):
- Add small heuristic check to CI to flag >20% increase in top-10 CPU symbols (owner: Diego).
- Expand eBPF traces that correlate queue wait times with callgraph samples (owner: Priya).
- Collect a small corpus of 30 representative failing traces and add to confluence examples (owner: Maya).

Notes to future readers:
- This is intentionally lightweight — if you need continuous low-overhead telemetry use our profiling-agent integration (see perf-agent docs).
- Keep flamegraphs as first-order triage; only escalate to full tracers and ETW-like instrumentation when necessary.

Quick links (internal):
- perf-agent repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-agent
- CI harvest job templates: https://gitlab.com/redwood-inference/ci-templates/-/blob/main/perf-harvest.yml
- Confluence guide (longform): confluence://eng/serving-runtime/profiling-bible

End of runbook.

Notes to self: polish the fold-and-flame script to normalize cgroup ids in paths and add optional anonymization for customer workloads before adding to public artifact store.
